content.title: What Is Energy?
content.explanation: Energy is the ability to do work or cause change. When you kick a ball, chemical energy in your muscles becomes kinetic energy in the ball. Energy can change form, but it never disappears!
keyPoints: Energy is the ability to do work
Energy can transform from one form to another
Energy is never created or destroyed (Law of Conservation)

content.title: Kinetic vs Potential Energy
content.explanation: A ball rolling down a hill has kinetic energy - energy of motion. A ball at the top of a hill has potential energy - stored energy waiting to be released. As the ball rolls down, potential energy converts to kinetic energy!
content.visualAlt: Ball at top of hill (potential) rolling down (kinetic)
keyPoints: Kinetic energy: energy of moving objects
Potential energy: stored energy (position, springs, chemicals)
Higher position = more gravitational potential energy
Faster speed = more kinetic energy

content.question: A stretched rubber band has what type of energy?
content.hint: Is the rubber band moving? Or is it storing energy, ready to be released?
content.explanationOnCorrect: Yes! Elastic potential energy is stored in the stretched band, waiting to be released as kinetic energy.
content.explanationOnWrong: Since the rubber band isn't moving yet, it has potential energy - stored energy ready to go.

content.question: True or False: When you eat food, you gain chemical potential energy that your body can use.
content.hint: Think about where your muscles get their energy from.
content.explanationOnCorrect: True! Food contains chemical potential energy stored in molecules. Your body breaks it down to power everything you do.
content.explanationOnWrong: Food contains chemical potential energy in its molecules. Your body converts it to kinetic energy for movement, heat, and more.

content.question: A boulder sits at the top of a cliff. As it falls, its potential energy ___.
content.hint: Energy doesn't disappear - it transforms. What is the boulder gaining as it falls?
content.explanationOnCorrect: Exactly! Potential energy converts to kinetic energy as the boulder falls and speeds up.
content.explanationOnWrong: As the boulder falls, gravitational potential energy converts into kinetic energy (motion). Energy is never destroyed!

content.title: Gravity and Gravitational Force
content.explanation: Gravity is a force that pulls objects with mass toward each other. The bigger the mass, the stronger the pull. Earth's gravity pulls you toward the ground. The Moon's gravity is 6 times weaker - that's why astronauts can jump so high on the Moon!
content.visualAlt: Earth pulling objects toward it with gravity arrows
keyPoints: Gravity is an attractive force between all objects with mass
More mass = stronger gravitational pull
Earth's gravity accelerates objects at 9.8 m/s²
Weight = mass × gravitational acceleration

content.title: Heat and Temperature
content.explanation: Temperature measures how fast particles are moving. Heat is the total energy of all those moving particles. A cup of boiling water has a higher temperature than a lake, but the lake has more total heat energy because it has billions more particles!
keyPoints: Temperature = average kinetic energy of particles
Heat = total thermal energy in a substance
Heat transfers from hot to cold objects
Measured in Celsius (°C) or Kelvin (K) in science

content.question: You weigh 50 kg on Earth. On the Moon (1/6 gravity), you would weigh approximately:
content.hint: If Moon gravity is 1/6 of Earth's, divide your Earth weight by 6.
content.explanationOnCorrect: Yes! 50 ÷ 6 ≈ 8.3 kg. You'd be much lighter but your mass stays the same - mass is how much 'stuff' you're made of.
content.explanationOnWrong: Moon gravity is 1/6 of Earth's. So 50 ÷ 6 ≈ 8.3 kg. Note: your mass stays 50 kg - only your weight changes!

content.question: Heat naturally flows from ___ objects to ___ objects.
content.hint: Put an ice cube in warm water. Which way does the temperature change?
content.explanationOnCorrect: Correct! Heat always flows from hotter to cooler objects until they reach the same temperature (thermal equilibrium).
content.explanationOnWrong: Heat flows from hot to cold. That's why ice cools your drink - heat from the drink flows into the ice.

content.question: Which has MORE total heat energy?
options: They have the same heat energy
content.hint: Temperature is average particle energy. Heat is TOTAL energy. Which has more particles?
content.explanationOnCorrect: Yes! Even though the cup is hotter, the pool has billions more particles. More particles × their energy = more total heat!
content.explanationOnWrong: The pool is cooler, but it has trillions more particles. Total heat = all particles × their energy, so the pool wins!

content.title: Electricity and Electric Circuits
content.explanation: Electricity is the flow of electrons through a material. When electrons flow through a wire, they carry electrical energy. A circuit gives electrons a complete path to flow. Break the circuit and electricity stops - that's how a light switch works!
content.visualAlt: Simple circuit with battery and light bulb
keyPoints: Electricity = flow of electrons
A circuit needs a complete path for electrons
Voltage is the 'push' driving electrons
Current is the amount of electron flow

content.title: Light and the Electromagnetic Spectrum
content.explanation: Light is electromagnetic energy that travels in waves. Visible light is just a tiny slice of the electromagnetic spectrum. Radio waves, microwaves, infrared (heat), X-rays, and gamma rays are all the same type of energy but with different wavelengths!
keyPoints: Light travels at 300,000 km per second
Different colors have different wavelengths (red = long, violet = short)
Radio waves, microwaves, X-rays are all electromagnetic waves
Higher frequency = more energy (X-rays have more than radio waves)

content.question: A light bulb converts electrical energy mainly into:
content.hint: Touch a light bulb after it's been on a while. What do you notice?
content.explanationOnCorrect: Correct! Light bulbs convert electricity into light AND heat. That's why they get warm. LED bulbs are better because they waste less energy as heat.
content.explanationOnWrong: Light bulbs produce both light AND heat. That's why incandescent bulbs feel hot. LEDs produce less heat.

content.question: Which type of electromagnetic wave has the MOST energy?
content.hint: Gamma rays can pass through most materials and are used in cancer treatment. Which does that suggest about their energy?
content.explanationOnCorrect: Yes! Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength and highest frequency, giving them the most energy. They're produced in nuclear reactions.
content.explanationOnWrong: Gamma rays have the highest frequency and shortest wavelength in the electromagnetic spectrum = most energy.

content.title: Newton's Three Laws of Motion
content.explanation: Isaac Newton figured out three rules for how forces and motion work. Law 1: Objects keep moving unless a force stops them (inertia). Law 2: Force = mass × acceleration. Law 3: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction - that's how rockets work!
keyPoints: 1st Law (Inertia): objects keep their state unless a force acts on them
2nd Law: F = ma (force = mass × acceleration)
3rd Law: For every action, there's an equal and opposite reaction
Rockets work by pushing gas down, which pushes the rocket up

content.question: A rocket pushes hot gases down. What happens to the rocket according to Newton's 3rd Law?
options: The rocket is pushed upward with equal force
correct: The rocket is pushed upward with equal force
content.hint: For every ACTION there is an equal and OPPOSITE reaction...
content.explanationOnCorrect: Exactly! The rocket pushes gases DOWN, so gases push the rocket UP. That's Newton's 3rd Law in action - literally!
content.explanationOnWrong: Newton's 3rd Law: every action = equal and opposite reaction. Gas goes down → rocket goes up!

content.question: Using F = ma: if a 2 kg ball accelerates at 5 m/s², what force is applied?
content.hint: F = m × a. Multiply mass times acceleration.
content.explanationOnCorrect: F = 2 kg × 5 m/s² = 10 N (Newtons). Newton's 2nd Law lets us calculate exactly how much force is needed!
content.explanationOnWrong: F = m × a. So F = 2 × 5 = 10 N. Newtons (N) are the unit of force.

content.title: Renewable vs Non-Renewable Energy
content.explanation: Fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas) are non-renewable - once burned, they're gone forever, and they took millions of years to form. Solar, wind, and hydroelectric power are renewable - they replenish naturally. Switching to renewables is key to fighting climate change!
keyPoints: Fossil fuels: coal, oil, natural gas - take millions of years to form
Burning fossil fuels releases CO₂ causing climate change
Renewable: solar, wind, hydroelectric, geothermal
Solar and wind are fastest growing energy sources

content.question: Which energy sources are renewable? (Select all that apply)
content.hint: Can the Sun stop shining or wind stop blowing? Can we make more coal quickly?
content.explanationOnCorrect: Yes! Solar and wind energy replenish naturally and constantly. Coal and natural gas are finite and take millions of years to form.
content.explanationOnWrong: Renewable means it naturally replenishes. The Sun keeps shining and wind keeps blowing. Coal and gas are finite fossil fuels.

content.question: Why do burning fossil fuels contribute to climate change?
options: They release CO₂ that traps heat in the atmosphere
They make the Sun shine brighter
They remove oxygen from the air
correct: They release CO₂ that traps heat in the atmosphere
content.hint: CO₂ acts like a blanket around Earth. What does a blanket do?
content.explanationOnCorrect: Exactly! CO₂ and other greenhouse gases trap heat from the Sun, causing Earth's average temperature to rise.
content.explanationOnWrong: Burning fossil fuels releases CO₂. In the atmosphere, CO₂ traps heat like a blanket, warming the planet.
